title: The Click Beside the Point: From a Pixel Back to a Sample, in Pixels and Not in Volts

questions.question: Time is on x, value on y. Which way does y go on a screen?
options: Down: a higher value is a smaller y
questions.explanation: The highest value was at y = 10 and the lowest at y = 90.

questions.question: Why is B picked and not A, when A is nearer in seconds and volts?
options: Nearness is measured in pixels, and a second and a volt are not the same size on the screen
questions.explanation: A was 40 pixels away and B 9.

questions.question: A click is exactly at the tolerance of 8 pixels. What happens?
options: The sample is picked: the tolerance is inclusive
questions.explanation: Exactly 8 picked it and 8.1 did not.

questions.question: What does pick return for a click on empty chart?
questions.explanation: A click on nothing should select nothing.

questions.question: Why can a sample outside the time shown not be picked?
options: It is not drawn: its pixel is off the chart, and a click there is not on the data
questions.explanation: Samples at -5 s and 105 s would be at x = -50 and 1050.

questions.question: What does from_pixel do with a usable width of zero?
options: Returns t0 for the time, without dividing
questions.explanation: It checks the size before dividing.
